physics.intuition: Physics looks for a compact set of rules that predict how the physical world changes.
physics.example: A falling ball connects motion, force, energy, measurement and mathematical modeling.

motion.intuition: Motion is change in position over time; the chosen reference frame matters.
motion.example: A train passenger can be at rest relative to the carriage and moving relative to the platform.

force.intuition: A force is an interaction that can change momentum; equal and opposite forces act on different objects.
force.example: A wheel pushes backward on the road, and the road pushes the wheel forward.

energy.intuition: Energy is a conserved accounting quantity. It can be transferred between systems or converted between forms.
energy.example: A falling object trades gravitational potential energy for kinetic energy.

temperature.intuition: Temperature describes thermal state; it is not the same thing as the energy transferred as heat.
temperature.example: A small hot cup can contain less total thermal energy than a cooler swimming pool.

heat.intuition: Heat means energy transfer driven by a temperature difference, not a substance stored in an object.
heat.example: Energy transfers from a hot pan into cooler water.

entropy.intuition: Entropy is a state quantity tied to how many microscopic configurations are compatible with a macroscopic state.
entropy.example: A gas spreading through a container has more accessible arrangements than gas confined to one corner.

thermodynamics.intuition: Thermodynamics relates heat, work and state changes without needing to follow every particle.
thermodynamics.example: An engine converts part of the energy received as heat into mechanical work, subject to limits.

statistical_mechanics.intuition: Statistical mechanics connects the behavior of many particles to measurable bulk properties.
statistical_mechanics.example: The average motion of enormous numbers of molecules helps explain gas pressure.

quantum_mechanics.intuition: Quantum mechanics models microscopic systems using states and probabilities; measurement outcomes are not classical trajectories.
quantum_mechanics.example: An atom absorbs light only at energies matching allowed transitions.

chemical_equilibrium.intuition: Equilibrium is dynamic: forward and reverse processes continue while their rates balance.
chemical_equilibrium.example: Molecules keep reacting in a sealed vessel even when overall concentrations stop changing.

physical_chemistry.intuition: Physical chemistry uses physical principles to understand chemical structure, transformations and bulk behavior.
physical_chemistry.example: Why does a reaction speed up when warmed, and how far can it proceed?

electromagnetism.intuition: Electric and magnetic fields describe a unified interaction between charges and currents.
electromagnetism.example: Changing magnetic fields induce electric effects in a generator.

fundamental_interaction.intuition: A fundamental interaction is one of the basic kinds of influence described in current physical theories.

natural_causes.intuition: Natural causes explain observations using processes that can be investigated rather than invoking supernatural agency.

atomism.intuition: Atomism proposes that matter is composed of discrete constituents; ancient atomism is historically distinct from modern atomic theory.

aristotelian_physics.intuition: A historical framework for motion and the cosmos, superseded in many predictions by later mechanics.

experimental_method.intuition: A way to test an explanation by measuring outcomes under controlled and reproducible conditions.

heliocentric_model.intuition: A model of the Solar System with the Sun near the center of planetary orbits, distinct from a model of the whole universe.

planetary_motion_laws.intuition: Empirical regularities of planetary orbits associated with Kepler, later explained through gravitation.

calculus.intuition: Mathematics of continuous change and accumulation, essential to many physics models.

cosmic_expansion.intuition: On large scales the separation between distant galaxies changes as space expands; it is not an explosion into pre-existing space.

radio_astronomy.intuition: Observational astronomy that measures radio-frequency radiation from celestial sources.

causal_determinism.intuition: The view that a system's state and dynamical laws uniquely determine later states; its applicability depends on the model.

systems_far_from_equilibrium.intuition: Systems maintained away from equilibrium by ongoing flows of matter or energy; equilibrium approximations may not describe them.

world_wide_web.intuition: A global information system linked by hypertext and the internet, included here as a historical application rather than a physics law.

reversibility.intuition: An ideal thermodynamic process that can be reversed without net change to the system and surroundings; real processes are typically irreversible.
